title: Privacy-R1: Privacy-Aware Multi-LLM Agent Collaboration via Reinforcement Learning
pdf_path: papers/Privacy-R1_Privacy-Aware Multi-LLM Agent Collaboration via Reinforcement Learning.pdf
threat_model_summary: A local model routes sentence chunks between local and remote LLMs to preserve task quality while limiting PII sent to the remote provider. Privacy is measured by exact PII string leakage, not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Privacy-Conscious Delegation as a sequential local/remote routing problem
Frozen MiniLM encoder plus Transformer policy, SFT warm start and PPO
Med-PCD dataset (1,020 examples) with human validation
89.5% quality / 5.1% leakage on Med-PCD with Llama-3.1-8B
limitations: Leakage metric is exact string matching
theoretical_crypto_links: Inference-game/DP-style leakage bounds are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, TEE, MPC or FHE
TLS/OAuth/log signatures cannot stop a remote provider from reading plaintext chunks (our inference)

title: When Personalization Legitimizes Risks: Uncovering Safety Vulnerabilities in Personalized Dialogue Agents
pdf_path: papers/When Personalization Legitimizes Risks_Uncovering Safety Vulnerabilities in Personalized Dialogue Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Benign accumulated user memories are retrieved during a harmful request and make the request appear contextually legitimate, lowering refusal. Not an adversarial prompt injection; no cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Intent legitimation: personalization lowers refusal for harmful requests
PS-Bench with 10 personas, 750 harmful queries and 5 safety benchmarks
15.8%-243.7% relative ASR increase across 5 memory frameworks and 5 LLMs
Detection-reflection intervention reduces ASR by about 27.4%
limitations: Some frameworks lose personalization utility under defense
theoretical_crypto_links: None; memory personalization is a semantic alignment problem
Memory access control/provenance is our inference and does not judge legitimacy
applied_crypto_links: At-rest memory encryption would not help because memories enter the prompt in plaintext (our inference)

title: Unintended Misalignment from Agentic Fine-Tuning: Risks and Mitigation
pdf_path: papers/Unintended Misalignment from Agentic Fine-Tuning_Risks and Mitigation.pdf
threat_model_summary: Benign agentic supervised fine-tuning can reduce refusal on harmful tasks without any adversarial data; PING adds a natural-language prefix at inference. Not an adversarial or cryptographic threat model.
core_contributions: Shows capability-safety trade-off from benign agentic fine-tuning across open and closed models
PING: iterative LLM-generated prefix search scored by non-refusal and refusal rates
Linear probe and activation steering analysis
Evaluation on Web navigation and code generation
limitations: Appendices A.1/C/D/E-G/H/I and Table 16 are absent from the 9-page PDF; hyperparameters/prompts/adversarial robustness not verifiable
PING is a prompt-level intervention, not a reference monitor
No adaptive bypass evaluation in the main text
theoretical_crypto_links: None; misalignment is a training/alignment phenomenon
applied_crypto_links: Model provenance/attestation cannot prove absence of misalignment (our inference)
blocking_issue: Referenced appendices and Table 16 are not included in the 9-page PDF; quality check incomplete for those details

title: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
pdf_path: papers/MATE_Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning.pdf
threat_model_summary: A post-hoc auditor judges whether a mobile agent trajectory violates app-specific policies; it is a supervised detector, not an enforcement point or cryptographic verifier.
core_contributions: MATE trajectory-level policy-conditioned auditor
158 apps, 934 policies, 140k synthetic labeled trajectories
Trajectory adapter and policy retriever for screenshots/UI trees
MATEBENCH IN/OUT/REAL and 95.06% REAL accuracy with 0.5B latency
limitations: Post-hoc judgment, not prevention or enforcement
Synthetic training data may not cover real policy drift
LLM-generated REAL labels and unclear human-level protocol
theoretical_crypto_links: None; auditing is supervised classification, not verifiable execution
Signed audit logs/attestation are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Signed trajectory logs could support provenance but not policy correctness (our inference)

title: MASLeak: Investigating and Exposing Intellectual Property Leakage Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Systems
pdf_path: papers/MASLeak_Investigating and Exposing Intellectual Property Leakage Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Systems.pdf
threat_model_summary: Black-box attacker queries only the first agent and observes the last agent's output; extracts agent count, topology, system prompts, task instructions and tool specs. No cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: First black-box IP extraction framework for multi-agent systems
Worm-like query decomposition qLeak/qRetain/qPropagate
810 synthetic MAS plus CrewAI/Coze evaluation
Extraction of topology/prompts/tools with 8.7 queries and <11 seconds on average
limitations: Synthetic ground truth and expert-built Coze apps
Defenses reduce but do not stop extraction
theoretical_crypto_links: None; IP leakage is semantic prompt extraction, not a cryptographic side channel
Query-budget leakage game/watermarking are our inference
applied_crypto_links: TEE/ACL cannot stop an agent from repeating its own prompt; watermarking only supports ownership detection (our inference)
